title: The Video Call You Can’t Trust
script: It is 2035. Your mother calls. Your phone says unverified. Her face looks right. Her voice sounds right. She says she needs money immediately. You almost tap send. Then you end the call and use the number you already know. Your mother answers. She is fine. The first call was someone else wearing her face. Watermarking and provenance tools exist today, but no universal badge can guarantee every caller is real. In a world of convincing copies, would you trust appearance alone?

directorBrief: Direct this as a human story about A convincing fake call forces a choice between appearance and proof of origin. Emotional movement: urgency → verification. Facts must be separately sourced; use a small persistent POSSIBLE FUTURE label, never a news-like breaking banner.

protocol: Produce original story assets, review factual grounding, verify every future claim is conditional or explicitly fictional, then inspect continuity and safe zones. No real-world experiment outcome is claimed.
